target_customer: Remote and hybrid company teams (HR and team leads)
problem: Remote teams lack social connection. Mixr ran virtual game tournaments and an ongoing office competition with built-in audio/video chat and leaderboards.
business_model: B2B SaaS for team engagement (pricing not found)
product_category: Remote team social and gaming platform

founders.name: Blaze Cerovcec
founders.background_notes: YC page lists one founder who describes himself as a software engineer.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time video chat, breakout rooms and leaderboards use standard WebRTC style components for a one-person team.

defensibility.rationale: Easily copied by Slack-based and virtual team-building tools; no sourced moat.

market_need_then: Remote and hybrid work in 2021 created demand for team-bonding tools, but no sourced spend data for Mixr.

branding.domain_note: Uses mixronline.com, not mixr.com; the shorter name is taken by other companies, including a separate MixR community software company.

brand_strength.rationale: Name collides with MixR (mixr.net), Mixlr, MixRift and others and the company needed an 'online' domain suffix; no sourced brand assets.

outcome_analysis: Mixr was a Summer 2021 YC company building game tournaments for remote teams, led by a single listed founder and a small team. YC lists it as inactive. No shutdown announcement, funding or post-mortem was found and mixronline.com returned HTTP 503, so the cause of the outcome is not public.
notes: Funding searches returned only different companies (MixR at mixr.net, MixRift, Mixlr); none attributed to this company. Alternatives pages (SaaSHub, Product Hunt: Switchboard, Pioneer, Human) are undated current listings, so no 2021 competitors recorded. One search snippet places the team in Toronto with team size 4, from an aggregator.
